title: Jacob and Esau Reconcile
text:
Twenty years earlier, Jacob had cheated his twin brother Esau twice: first buying his birthright for a bowl of stew, then tricking their blind father Isaac into giving him the blessing meant for Esau. Esau swore he would kill him, and Jacob fled to his uncle Laban in Haran.

Now Jacob was coming home with wives, children and flocks, and messengers brought word that Esau was coming to meet him with four hundred men. Jacob was terrified. He divided his household into two camps, prayed, and sent ahead wave after wave of gifts: goats, sheep, camels, cows and donkeys, hundreds of animals, with servants instructed to tell Esau they were a present from his servant Jacob.

That night, alone by the ford of the Jabbok, Jacob wrestled with a mysterious man until dawn and came away limping, with a new name, Israel.

In the morning he saw Esau approaching. Jacob went ahead of his family and bowed to the ground seven times as he approached his brother. But Esau ran to meet him, embraced him, threw his arms around his neck and kissed him, and they wept. Esau at first refused the gifts: "I have enough, my brother." Jacob pressed him, saying that seeing his face was like seeing the face of God, now that Esau had received him so kindly. Esau accepted, and the two brothers parted in peace.
lesson: Old wrongs between siblings can be healed if one comes humbly and the other chooses generosity. Make the first move, even if you are afraid.
